title: catch for str() in column proxy is not catching unsupported custom SQL constructs
body:
**Describe the bug**
We have update to sqlalchemy version 1.3.22 but now a custom compile function doesn't work anymore. Before it worked fine in 1.2.14.

I already debugged the issue and it seems while compiling the custom function, the dialect and/or bind get's lost and therefore sqlalchemy falls back to the default SQL string compiler which cannot compile the function (by purpose on my side).

**Expected behavior**
The custom compile function should work again.

```sql
SELECT anon_1."TableA_create_date" AS "anon_1_TableA_create_date", anon_1."TableA_create_time" AS "anon_1_TableA_create_time", anon_1."TableA_id" AS "anon_1_TableA_id", anon_1.create_timestamp AS anon_1_create_timestamp, "MappingTable_1".id AS "MappingTable_1_id", "MappingTable_1".value_a AS "MappingTable_1_value_a", "MappingTable_1".value_b AS "MappingTable_1_value_b" 
FROM (SELECT "TableA".create_date AS "TableA_create_date", "TableA".create_time AS "TableA_create_time", "TableA".id AS "TableA_id", datetime("TableA".create_date, "TableA".create_time) AS create_timestamp 
FROM "TableA" JOIN "MappingTable" ON "TableA".id = "MappingTable".value_a JOIN "TableB" ON "TableB".id = "MappingTable".value_b 
WHERE "TableB".base_value = ? AND "MappingTable".value_b = ? ORDER BY create_timestamp DESC
 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?) AS anon_1 LEFT OUTER JOIN "MappingTable" AS "MappingTable_1" ON anon_1."TableA_id" = "MappingTable_1".value_a ORDER BY anon_1.create_timestamp DESC
```

**To Reproduce**
```py
# pylint: disable=no-member

from datetime import datetime

import pytz

from sqlalchemy.engine import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, Date, Time, Unicode, ForeignKey, DateTime
from sqlalchemy.sql import expression
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, joinedload, relationship
from sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid import hybrid_property
from sqlalchemy.ext.compiler import compiles


Base = declarative_base()


class BaseTable(Base):
    __tablename__ = "BaseTable"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True,)


class TableA(Base):
    __tablename__ = "TableA"

    id = Column(Integer, unique=True, primary_key=True)
    problem_mappings = relationship("MappingTable")

    _create_date = Column("create_date", Date)
    _create_time = Column("create_time", Time)

    @hybrid_property
    def create_time(self):
        return datetime.combine(self._create_date, self._create_time, tzinfo=pytz.UTC)

    @create_time.expression
    def create_time(self):
        return combine_date_time(self._create_date, self._create_time).label(
            "create_timestamp"
        )


class TableB(Base):
    __tablename__ = "TableB"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    base_value = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(BaseTable.id))


class MappingTable(Base):
    __tablename__ = "MappingTable"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    value_a = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(TableA.id))
    value_b = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(TableB.id))


class combine_date_time(expression.FunctionElement):
    name = "datetime"
    type = DateTime()


@compiles(combine_date_time, "sqlite")
def sqlite_combine_date_time(element, compiler, **kw):
    return "datetime(%s)" % compiler.process(element.clauses, **kw)


def main():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)()

    result = (
        session.query(TableA)
        .join(MappingTable)
        .join(TableB)
        .filter(TableB.base_value == 1, MappingTable.value_b == 1,)
        .order_by(TableA.create_time.desc())
        .limit(50)
        .options(joinedload(TableA.problem_mappings))
    )

    print(result)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
